summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the Islamic obligation of parents to teach their children prayer beginning at age seven, based on a hadith narrated on the authority of Ali. He emphasizes that this is not merely a suggestion but a serious religious duty, explaining that children should learn to pray with full Islamic etiquette including proper covering and ablution by age seven, and that physical discipline may be employed by age ten if they fail to comply. Sh. Ali Mashhour addresses contemporary Western ideologies that discourage parental guidance, arguing that children lack the capacity for independent thought and will absorb values from their environment regardless—making parental responsibility crucial in shaping their Islamic identity and obedience to Allah.
suggested_title: Teaching Children Prayer and Islamic Discipline: Parental Obligations and Responsibilities
catchy_title: Why Parents Must Command Their Children to Pray
hadith_chapter: Narration on the authority of Ali regarding children and prayer
